question: ap1
constraint: without any genetic perturbation (no knockouts, knockdowns, CRISPR, or overexpression)
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out without any genetic perturbation (no knockouts, knockdowns, CRISPR, or overexpression). Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Pulse-washout-rechallenge chromatin time course
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief, defined stimulus pulse (e.g. TNF, serum, or a MEK inhibitor), wash it out, and then profile ATAC-seq plus CUT&RUN for Fos/Jun family members at a dense series of timepoints spanning hours to weeks after washout. Memory is supported if a subset of AP-1-bound accessible regions remains open long after AP-1 protein levels and upstream signaling have returned to baseline, and if rechallenge produces a faster or larger response specifically at those retained sites.

ideas.title: Live-cell AP-1 reporter lineage tracing through division
ideas.description: Use a non-integrating or pre-existing AP-1 activity reporter line and long-term live imaging to track individual cells and their progeny through many divisions, quantifying how reporter intensity correlates between mother and daughter and between sisters as a function of elapsed time. The decay constant of this correlation gives a direct, model-free measurement of how long AP-1 state information persists and whether it survives mitosis, which is the defining test of heritable memory versus transient signaling.

ideas.title: Pharmacological clamp-and-release to separate maintenance from establishment
ideas.description: Use small-molecule AP-1 inhibitors (e.g. T-5224 or a JNK inhibitor) applied either only during the initial stimulus or only during the post-stimulus memory window, then assay the response to a later rechallenge. If blocking AP-1 during establishment abolishes memory but blocking it afterward does not, AP-1 writes the memory; if blocking it during the window also erases memory, AP-1 is required continuously to maintain it, which distinguishes a writer from a self-sustaining latch.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome correlation of AP-1 motif accessibility with response history
ideas.description: Perform joint single-cell ATAC and RNA profiling on a population carrying heterogeneous stimulus histories (created by staggered pulse timing or by sorting cells on an early response reporter), and ask whether per-cell AP-1 motif accessibility scores predict that cell's transcriptional response to a subsequent challenge. A strong single-cell predictive relationship, stronger than that for other motif families, would show AP-1 chromatin state is the physical carrier of the remembered information rather than a correlate of it.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and post-mitotic reestablishment kinetics
ideas.description: Synchronize cells pharmacologically (e.g. thymidine block and release, or nocodazole arrest), then measure AP-1 factor retention on mitotic chromosomes by imaging and by CUT&RUN on sorted mitotic and early-G1 cells, tracking how quickly accessibility and transcription are restored at previously induced loci. Retention of a subset of AP-1 on condensed chromatin plus accelerated reactivation of exactly those loci in G1 would provide a concrete molecular mechanism for how the memory crosses cell division.
